page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 CPU architecture. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core.

This server type does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, making it reliant on network-attached storage options for persistent data. It also does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Given its arm64 architecture and dedicated CPU allocation, the c4a-highcpu-8 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that benefit from a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration makes it suitable for stateless applications, microservices, containerized APIs, and lightweight CI/CD pipelines that require dedicated processing power without high memory or local storage requirements.
